游戏底子不错，虽然不算是原创但是同类里没多少能打的，玩倒是能玩，但是几个致命问题不得不打差评 1.声音，这全部是其他游戏偷来的音效我就不较真了，但是连个音量大小选项都不给？而且不知道这游戏是哪根筋抽了我在steam混合器里调音量甚至不能把这游戏的声音关了，这么基础的bug我甚至怀疑是态度问题了 2.游戏描述，举个最明显的例子，两个增益道具的描述是周围物理/能量武器伤害增加，结果点进武器图鉴里没有一个武器写着物理/能量，我是不知道你这火箭是爆炸喷火器是穿透吗？而且数值描述更是偷懒，这类游戏最有深度的玩法是自己拿着计算器算数值而不是抄别人试出来的作业，结果除了武器本身的伤害攻速完全不写详细，根本算不了 3.局内成长极其不合理，这类游戏的核心一直都是围绕格子，结果这游戏的格子居然不能稳定成长，换其他游戏通关是稳定给格子，到了这游戏里是稳定给银币，结果就是连打3关被格子卡得0提升，你要是每次刷新都稳定出格子我都当这游戏不想搞人心态了，更搞人心态的是该有仓检的地方没有，其他这类游戏武器一般都能旋转，结果这游戏里武器不能旋转就算了格子也不行，喜欢我还剩最后3个连着的横格子连着几关没提升结果刷出个竖着的格子吗，这换个心态不好的玩家当场就删游戏了

It is a fun game well worth its cost. However right now it is not worth it to play past a certain point, due to horrible balancing issues. The starting weapons outperform anything you unlock in the game by a huge margin, and take up less space to boot. You end up building the same tank every single game, or loose if you draw too many of the new weapons. The new weapons also don't have any cards to boost them, the laser should be able to be hooked up to the battery, like the flamer is hooked up to the fuel tank etc. The balancing on the level up cards is ridiculus. The macine gun gets +50% crit chance, and the flamer +100% damage, while the new weapons have some paltry +15% damage in comparison.
What a delightful time-waster! Highly recommended

Thunder Tank: Iron Shield is a post-apocalyptic action game that combines twin-stick shooting, roguelite progression, idle mechanics, and strategic inventory management into a single experience. Developed and published by Crazy Studio, the game places players behind the controls of a heavily armed combat tank tasked with surviving increasingly dangerous waves of enemies across a devastated world. Rather than focusing solely on reflex-based combat, it emphasizes planning, experimentation, and long-term progression, making each battle part of a larger journey toward building the ultimate armored war machine. One of the game's defining mechanics is its backpack-inspired equipment system, which transforms weapon management into a strategic puzzle. Every gun, turret, and support device occupies valuable space inside the tank, forcing players to carefully arrange their loadout before entering combat. Choosing between rapid-fire machine guns, explosive rocket launchers, devastating heavy cannons, piercing laser weapons, flamethrowers, and electric shock towers requires more than simply selecting the strongest option. Their size, positioning, and synergy all influence overall effectiveness, rewarding players who enjoy optimizing builds and discovering combinations that maximize both offense and defense. Combat is fast-paced without sacrificing tactical depth. Enemies attack in overwhelming numbers, filling the battlefield with constant threats that demand careful movement and intelligent positioning. Although the action features familiar bullet-hell elements, victory is often determined before the battle even begins through thoughtful preparation and equipment choices. Every successful run encourages players to refine their strategies, while failed attempts still contribute to future progress by providing valuable resources that can be invested in permanent upgrades. The progression system is designed to make every session worthwhile. Resources collected during missions can be used to improve weapons, unlock stronger equipment, enhance the tank's overall performance, and acquire new abilities. The inclusion of idle progression ensures that advancement continues steadily, reducing frustration while maintaining a satisfying sense of accomplishment. This balance makes the game approachable for casual players who prefer shorter play sessions while still providing enough depth for those who enjoy experimenting with increasingly efficient builds. Replay value is strengthened through multiple unlockable tanks, each offering unique characteristics and specialized skill trees. Instead of functioning as simple cosmetic variations, these vehicles encourage different approaches to combat by emphasizing specific strengths such as raw firepower, survivability, or resource efficiency. Combined with twenty escalating difficulty levels, players are consistently challenged to adapt their strategies and optimize their equipment layouts to overcome tougher enemy encounters. The growing variety of builds keeps progression engaging long after the opening stages. Visually, Thunder Tank: Iron Shield embraces a gritty post-apocalyptic atmosphere filled with ruined cities, abandoned industrial facilities, and desolate wastelands. While the graphics favor clarity over technical spectacle, the clean visual presentation allows players to easily track enemy movements, weapon effects, and incoming projectiles even during the most chaotic firefights. The straightforward art direction effectively supports gameplay by ensuring that readability is never compromised during intense action. Despite its engaging mechanics, the game does have a few limitations. The overall gameplay loop remains focused on surviving enemy waves and upgrading equipment, which may begin to feel repetitive during extended sessions for players seeking greater mission variety or a stronger narrative experience. Some quality-of-life improvements and interface refinements could further improve accessibility, although the core gameplay remains enjoyable thanks to its satisfying progression systems and strategic customization. Overall, Thunder Tank: Iron Shield delivers an enjoyable blend of action, strategy, and progression that successfully combines several modern gameplay concepts into a cohesive package. Its emphasis on weapon management, thoughtful build creation, rewarding upgrades, and increasingly demanding combat creates a compelling experience that appeals to fans of roguelites, idle progression, and tactical shooters alike. While it may not reinvent the genre, it offers enough depth and replayability to remain entertaining across many hours of play. Rating: 8/10

Ok, this is a very cheaap game, so it is worth the money. That being said, it is a very simple and short game, basicaly it is one of those Ad games for mobile. Don't expect anything else or you will be disapointed. Pros: The game uses the same art of metal slug it looks and sounds great most of the time The backpack hero mecanic of building your tank is fun. Cons: Bugs, bugs everwhere... Even the last boss, to simulate 4 legs the dev used 2 sprites that move out of sync, the problem is that you will also see 2 torsos (this is just an example) Game balance. There is none, if you play until ate least wave 5 you will notice how bad it is, if you survive the 2-3 waves of a map you already won. And some maps are completely insane how hard those waves are, the it gets completely trivial. Also the games gets ridiculouly easy after wave 8ish. You will be playing the exact 6 maps over and over again, and they are very short. Gets repetitive very fast, I just put that many hours because i want to be fair on this review and make sure that i was not mistaken. And no, the game never changes. Quality is also not there, the targeting AI is super dumb, this game was either the first project of a new developer (witch is fine) or was made in a rush with no quality at all. I bet i have more pllay time than the dev codding this game. All that being said it is still a fun game, but it has so much wasted potential... I am giving this a pass because you will have at least 2-10h of fun playing it, and for the price it is worth it.

For cheap, this is a Hell of an auto-battler. The game to play involves, as with God Of War, arranging equipment and weapons in an abstract tank "box". Duplicates level up equipment and weapons. Then one sits back and watches your tank attempt to side-scroll/plow through the enemies. At first you might be disappointed by what looks like only a few mission sections, but worry not, the game has more to offer. Great little game.

Good idea, could have been a good game, but the stategy every time just ends up being restart a level over and over until the game finally gives you enough machine guns, and then proceed to breeze through. If you get past round 2 you'll get past round 10 without a problem...
Cool, fun game.. would like more content, but definitely can't complain for what you get for this price.
Great cheap game

The game offers a refreshing blend of idling and tactical gameplay. Crafting my tank and experimenting with various weapons keeps me invested through the 20 difficulty levels.
While the core mechanics are promising, the game's balance could be improved. The weapon variety and synergy feel somewhat limited, but it's a solid casual title nonetheless.

Addictive mix of bullet chaos and smart loadout planning. Building the perfect setup, unlocking new gear, and watching your tank evolve makes every run feel satisfying and fun.
Thunder Tank offers a decent mix of strategy and casual gameplay, though it feels somewhat shallow after a few hours. Worth a try for the price.
Fit guns like Tetris pieces into your tank's inventory while it auto-fires at wasteland enemies. A chill shooter with grindy upgrades.
I really enjoy the tank customization aspect. It's fun to mix and match weapons in the limited slots while blasting through waves of enemies in the wasteland.
Pilot a battle vehicle through 20 difficulty levels in this post-apocalyptic idle bullet hell. Manage 13 unique weapons within a limited grid, unlock specialized tanks, and grow stronger via idling.
Backpack Hero with high-octane tank combat in a jolly mix of inventory management and side-scrolling idle shooter. Strategically fit weapons into your limited tank grid and survive all enemy waves!
